record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: In supersymmetric models with conserved R-parity or matter parity, the lightest supersymmetric particle is stable and can be a cosmological relic. Which MSSM particle, if any, supplies the non-baryonic dark matter—especially among sneutrinos and neutralinos with bino, wino, or higgsino components—and can accelerator measurements and direct dark-matter searches verify that the same stable particle accounts for the cosmic dark matter density?

evidence.quote: Question #10 How does SUSY shed light on dark matter?
In supersymmetric models with R-parity (or matter-parity) conservation, sparticles can only interact in pairs, thereby guaranteeing that the lightest SUSY particle (LSP) is absolutely stable.
The MSSM provides two ideal candidates for the dark matter, both of them WIMP’s: the sneutrino and the neutralino.
It may be possible to study the dark matter candidate both at accelerators and in dark matter detectors, hopefully verifying that the properties observed in one match those seen in the other.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) with exact R-parity (equivalently, matter parity) conservation, in which superpartners can be produced and destroyed only in pairs and the lightest supersymmetric particle (LSP) is therefore absolutely stable. Such an LSP, if electrically and color neutral, is a candidate weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) that may constitute the non-baryonic cold dark matter of the universe. The two natural neutral LSP candidates in the MSSM are: (i) the sneutrino ν̃ (the scalar superpartner of a Standard Model neutrino), and (ii) the lightest neutralino χ̃₁⁰, defined as the lightest mass eigenstate of the 4×4 neutralino mass matrix mixing the bino B̃, the neutral wino W̃³, and the two neutral higgsinos H̃_u⁰, H̃_d⁰.

Tasks:
(a) Determine which (if any) of these MSSM particles can supply the observed cosmological cold dark matter density Ω_DM h² ≈ 0.12, specifying for the neutralino case the admissible bino/wino/higgsino composition and mass range consistent with thermal relic abundance, with direct-detection bounds on the spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon cross sections, with indirect-detection limits, and with collider constraints on superpartner masses.
(b) Describe an experimental program by which accelerator measurements of the LSP's mass, spin, couplings, and annihilation cross sections, together with independent measurements in direct (and indirect) dark-matter detection experiments, would allow one to verify that the stable particle produced and inferred at colliders is the same particle that accounts for the cosmic dark matter density, including a quantitative criterion for "matching" between collider-inferred and astrophysically inferred properties.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, the identity of the dark matter particle remains experimentally unresolved. Sneutrino LSP dark matter is essentially excluded by direct-detection limits (XENON-1T, LZ, PandaX-4T) combined with the invisible Z width. The neutralino LSP remains a viable candidate, but recent LZ 2024/2025 spin-independent limits, LHC Run 3 searches, and phenomenological MSSM scans have strongly constrained the bino/wino/higgsino parameter space without confirming or ruling out neutralino dark matter. No accelerator has yet produced superpartners, so the cross-verification program envisioned has not been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Current status of the light neutralino thermal dark matter in the phenomenological MSSM
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results from dark matter and collider experiments put strong constraints on light neutralino thermal dark matter scenarios in the pMSSM.
status_evidence.claim: Neutralino dark matter remains a constrained but viable scenario as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: The Light Neutralino Dark Matter at Future Colliders in the MSSM
status_evidence.snippet: Future colliders such as FCCee and CEPC are expected to probe surviving regions of MSSM neutralino dark matter parameter space.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether the neutralino is the dark matter is not resolved and awaits future experiments.
